module Base
{
    /* Red Fox -- generated by tools/write_definitions.py.

       These animals carry their OWN skeleton, fitted to the mesh rather than
       the other way round (tools/fit_skeleton.py). So each model names its own
       animationsMesh, whose meshFile is this same .glb -- meshFile IS the
       animation skeleton, and naming the vanilla one is what forced our meshes
       into the donor's bind pose. See SKELETON-PLAN.md.

       The bones keep their vanilla NAMES, which is what lets Raccoon's clips
       still drive them: the engine binds animation to skeleton by name at every
       stage. */

    model KWC_Fox
    {
        mesh = Skinned/KWC_Fox,
        shader = animalEffect,
        static = false,
        animationsMesh = KWC_Fox_Anim,
    }

    animationsMesh KWC_Fox_Anim
    {
        meshFile = Skinned/KWC_Fox,
        keepMeshAnimations = true,
    }

    model KWC_FoxKit
    {
        mesh = Skinned/KWC_FoxKit,
        shader = animalEffect,
        static = false,
        animationsMesh = KWC_FoxKit_Anim,
    }

    animationsMesh KWC_FoxKit_Anim
    {
        meshFile = Skinned/KWC_FoxKit,
        keepMeshAnimations = true,
    }

}
